question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $P?$

I. $P∨(Q∧P)$

II. $(Q∧P)∨P$

III. $P∨(Q∨P)$
question.worked_solution:
The law that disjunction absorbs conjunction is stated as

$$
P∨(P∧Q)≡P.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is logically equivalent to $P.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∨(Q∧P) & ≡P∨(P∧Q) \\  & ≡P.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $P.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(Q∧P)∨P & ≡P∨(Q∧P) \\  & ≡P∨(P∧Q) \\  & ≡P.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is *not* logically equivalent to $P.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
